column1: # deb-native syscall catalog -- the exact, categorized list of the syscalls
# the runtime overlay handles (docs/spec/overlay.md, "The shared filter's
# rules").  One source of truth: the build embeds it in dn-trace verbatim
# gate-IP exemption from the gate=yes rows; dn-glibc wires the glibc=yes rows,
# and a repo check keeps the two in step (principle 1: one place the rules
# PROVENANCE / SCOPE -- this list is NOT universal; it follows the Android
# kernel and Android policy, so read it with its version:
#   android:  12 (kernel string "android12-9"; recheck per device/API level)
#   sources:  docs/spec/overlay.md ("The shared filter's rules" -- the
# epoll_pwait2 and SysV IPC -> real substitutes, the setuid/... "0" bucket)
# is a dn-glibc-android.patch concern, not an overlay one; it lives in that
# patch's fakesyscall.json, which is the companion to this file.
# Columns: syscall  group  handling  glibc  gate
#   group    path | identity   (everything else is "other": always ALLOWed)
#   handling what dn-policy must do, comma-separated:
#            map | resolve | fake-stat | fake-ids | fake-owner | link2symlink |
#   glibc    yes = dn-glibc translates/rewrites it in-process
#   gate     yes = dn-glibc issues its kernel call from the gate page, so the
#            filter may ALLOW it -- only when EVERY libc entry point issuing
#            it translates (a syscalls.list-generated wrapper such as
#            unlinkat() does not, so unlinkat is "no" even though unlink() is
#            wired); no = it is TRACEd and ptrace handles it
#            (a `no` row is still correct, just slower).  The filter's rule:
#            TRACE every path/identity call, except ALLOW one with gate=yes
#            that really came from the gate page.
